interview_room.situation: The lead interviewer looks up from your resume and asks: 'Tell me about a time you faced a difficult bug in your final-year project.'
interview_room.choiceA: I usually ask my batchmates or senior to fix hard bugs for me so I don't waste project time.
interview_room.choiceB: I isolate the module with unit tests, reproduce the error in debug mode, and systematically inspect the call stack before patching.
interview_room.choiceC: Bugs happen all the time, honestly I just rewrite the whole code block until it works.

feedbacks.A: Shows lack of individual problem-solving ownership.
feedbacks.B: Demonstrates structured engineering methodology and technical maturity.
feedbacks.C: Trial-and-error without root cause analysis is seen as inefficient.

tips.A: Highlight how you debug independently before asking for guidance.
tips.B: Maintain this STAR structure (Situation, Task, Action, Result) in your answers.
tips.C: Explain your systematic debugging steps rather than rewriting blindly.

interview_room.situation: The interviewer remarks: 'Your academic score in 3rd semester dipped a bit. What happened there?'
interview_room.choiceA: The university professors were setting very unfair question papers that semester.
interview_room.choiceB: I was balancing a robotics competition and time management slipped, but I rebuilt my study schedule and brought my GPA back to 8.4.
interview_room.choiceC: I didn't really like the subjects in that semester, so I didn't study much.

feedbacks.A: Blaming external factors leaves a very poor impression.
feedbacks.B: Owns the mistake, shows resilience and a verified turnaround.
feedbacks.C: Suggests low discipline when working on uninteresting assignments.

tips.A: Never blame teachers or college; take accountability.
tips.B: Great job pivoting from a setback to a positive recovery story.
tips.C: Show willingness to deliver excellence even on tough or dry topics.

interview_room.situation: Do you have any questions for us before we wrap up?
interview_room.choiceA: No sir, nothing from my side, I just want to know my package and salary.
interview_room.choiceB: Could you share what technologies the team is adopting this quarter and what mentorship a fresher receives?
interview_room.choiceC: When will I get the offer letter?

feedbacks.A: Focusing solely on compensation at round 1 sounds transactional.
feedbacks.B: Demonstrates genuine curiosity about team culture and growth.
feedbacks.C: Presumptuous and skips learning about the actual role.

tips.A: Save salary queries for HR round; ask role-specific questions here.
tips.B: Asking about team roadmap leaves a strong lasting impression.
tips.C: Inquire about onboarding and tech stack instead.

office_floor.situation: You notice your pull request has 12 review comments from a senior engineer pointing out naming convention flaws.
office_floor.choiceA: Reply 'looks fine to me' and merge the branch anyway.
office_floor.choiceB: Acknowledge the feedback, comment on each thread with your fixes, and ask for a 5-minute sync if any point is unclear.
office_floor.choiceC: Complain to the team lead that the senior engineer is nitpicking.

feedbacks.A: Merging unapproved code breaks team trust and CI/CD policy.
feedbacks.B: Professional, constructive, and respects code quality standards.
feedbacks.C: Creates workplace friction over standard engineering guidelines.

tips.A: Never bypass branch protection or peer reviews.
tips.B: Clear communication in PR comments saves hours of debugging.
tips.C: Treat code reviews as learning opportunities, not attacks.

office_floor.situation: You finish your assigned ticket 2 days ahead of the sprint deadline.
office_floor.choiceA: Browse social media quietly until sprint review.
office_floor.choiceB: Notify your scrum master, document your work, and offer to pick up a backlog bug or assist a teammate.
office_floor.choiceC: Leave office early without telling anyone.

feedbacks.B: High initiative, teamwork, and proactive communication.
feedbacks.C: Serious attendance violation on an internship or job.

tips.A: Use extra sprint time to write tests or learn new tooling.
tips.B: Proactivity is the #1 trait leads look for in junior hires.
tips.C: Always communicate your status with your manager.

wardrobe.situation: You are preparing for a virtual technical interview with an enterprise bank.
wardrobe.choiceA: A wrinkle-free button-down shirt/formal kurta, neutral background, and proper lighting.
wardrobe.choiceB: A bright hooded sweatshirt with loud graphics.
wardrobe.choiceC: Formal shirt on top, pajama bottoms, sitting in a dimly lit bedroom with bed visible.

feedbacks.A: Crisp professional appearance and camera framing.
feedbacks.B: Too casual for a banking/finance enterprise culture.
feedbacks.C: Messy background and poor lighting distract from your technical answers.

tips.A: Solid colors and natural face lighting convey high professionalism.
tips.B: Research company culture beforehand; banking expects business formal.
tips.C: Clean your camera background and sit upright in proper attire.
